findings.passage: "As I meet and talk with constituents in our area and across our state, election security is top of mind," Sweet said.
findings.note: Press release from the Indiana House caucus quoting her on why she filed a bill on how ballots are cast and counted. Related election-integrity material, not about ID.

House Bill 1286, the Trust and Transparency in Elections Act, would remove electronic voting machines, electronic poll books and ballot marking devices and require hand-marked, hand-counted paper ballots made in Indiana with a watermark and serial numbers. The release says it was assigned to the House Elections and Apportionment Committee. Related election-integrity bill, not about ID.

findings.passage: Sweet said to register, Indiana residents must be at least 18 years old on or before the upcoming election, have a valid Indiana Driver's License or Indiana State Identification Card, be a citizen of the United States, have lived in the same precinct for at least 30 days before the next election, and not currently imprisoned after being convicted of a crime.
findings.note: Caucus press release in her name listing the requirements to register in Indiana, including a state license or state ID card and US citizenship. It describes existing rules and takes no side on changing them.
subjects: ID needed to register to vote

findings.passage: "IndianaVoters.com is your one-stop-shop when it comes to information about voting and Election Day," Sweet said.
findings.note: Same release; she points voters to the state site, which she says also explains how Indiana works to keep elections safe and secure.

Senate Bill 137 (2025), titled 'Voter registration.' The bill history lists her as House sponsor, with two other House members as cosponsors. It became Public Law 72 on 2025-04-16. The tracker page does not give the bill text, so what the bill changes is not confirmed here.
